PennGlobal: PMR198
Period: VS 1148 and 1127
Location: Rājpur
King: Raṇadhavala
Dynasty: Paramāra
Language: Sanskrit
Script: Nagari
Text:  Prose and Metrical in 12 verses
Metres: Verses 1-2, 4-5, 9-10 Anuṣṭubh; vv. 3, 7, 11 Vasantatilakā; v.6 Indravajrā; v.8 Śālinī; v.12
	    Puṣpitāgrā
Gist: Records the donation of the village Madudahā by the subordinate prince. 
	Grant was issued by  Raṇadhavaia after bathing at the confluence of the Rēva and the Kapilā, 
	for the spiritual benefist of his parents and himself.
Published reference: Trivedi (1989), no. 198.



Text{1}
	    

First Plate

   sāsaneḥ{3} kalyāṇama-

30. ṭikāmalake[tyādi]{20} kasamastādāyatalādyādisarvvādāyairupeta[śca]raṇauprakṣā-
31. lya mātāpitro[rātma]naśca puṇyayaso(śo)'[bhivṛddha]ye{21} sā(śā)sanaṃ kṛtvodakapūrvva-
32. katvanena(katvena) pradattaḥ | satahavaṃ(tta)ri{22}tyadhikaikādaśaśatasaṃvatsarāṃtarggatacaitraśu-
33. di navamyāṃ mahākṣapaṭalā[kutnā]ryaśrījaye bhāṃḍāgārai(re) niva(ba)ddhā(ddhaḥ){23}| punama(rma)yākṣa-
34. ṭala[sā(śā)]sanaṃ kārayitvā āmā(gā?)misu(śu)ddhaḥ [nṛ]patiparijānīya{24} śrīmahārājādhirā-

Third Plate

45. pālanaṃ ca ||7|| sarvvānetānbhāvinaḥ pārthiveṃdrāṃ{27}bhūyo bhūyo yācate rāmabha-
46. draḥ | sāmānyoyaṃ dharmmaseturnṛpāṇāṃ kāle kāle pālanīyo bhavadbhiḥ ||8|| svadattāṃ pa-
47. radattāṃ vā yo haretu(ta) vasuṃdharāṃ(rām) | ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi viṣṭhāyāṃ yā(jā)yate kṛmiḥ ||9||
48. svadattāṃ paradattāṃ vā yo'nupālayate mahīṃ(hīm) | ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasā(srā)ṇi sve(sva)rggaloke

50. ki(vi)[bhū]pāḥ | ye pālayaṃti mama dhamma(rmma)mahaṃ nu mepāṃ(teṣāṃ) pādāraviṃdayugalaṃ si(śi)rasā na

53. saṃvat 1177 caitra śudi 9 gurau | dū.{29} puro[hi]taśrīvāmanasvāmi |{30} rāja-
54. putrakumārapālau | maṃgalaṃ mahāśrī[ḥ*] ||
55. ra śrīḥ [||?] so | saṃ || [nṛ] rā | 6 śa[ṭapā ?] 3 [||?]
56. sva[ha]stoyaṃ{31} mahārājādhirājaparamesva(śva)raśrīmannaravarmmadevasya ||{32}

----------------------------------------------------------------------

{1} From the original plates.
{2} Expressed by a symbol.
{3} Read smarārāteḥ, as the other charters of the house. The first of these akṣaras is omitted; the forms of 
	the second and the third are changed by a redundant horizontal stroke in each; and the consonant of 
	the fourth is engraved as n.
{4} Read mahārāja-.
{5} Sandhi between the first two akṣaras in this line, as also in some instances below, is not observed.
{6} The anusvāra is redundant. The hyphen is used by me to denote the end of one title. The preceding
	sya is not necessary in the samāsa.
{7} The reading is uncertain. Probably to be restored as ante (near its end), or antar-(inside it).
{8} The same as Drāṅgikā, i.e., the officer in charge of a town, for which cf. the Ūnā inscription, Ep. Ind.,
	Vol. IX, pp.4f. Also see C. I. I., Vol. III, p. 169, n. 6. Or, with the supply of u at the beginning,
	Udraṅga variṣṭha, i.e., an officer who collected levy. Cf. C. I. I., Vol. III, p.97, and n.
{9} The letters in the brackets have left only traces. The use of the initial i in viṣaika that follows is 
	noteworthy, instead of yi.
{10} The sign of visarga, which can be seen only on the original, was inserted later on. The daṇḍa that
	 follows is redundant. 
{11} The bracketed akṣara is formed as Yaṁ.
{12} Read patimumā-. A redundant daṇḍa is engraved after pū that follows.
{13} Probably what is intended is śāntis. The five śāntis, to propitiate the grahas, pitṛs, bhūtas, devās,
	 and bhahman.
{14} Read dadusteṣāṃ.
{15} The daṇḍa in this and the following lines are redundant. 
{16} Read kauṇḍinya.
{17} The daṇḍa is engraved as a pṛṣṭha mātrā of the following latter. This śākhā is not known to me.
	 Probably Vājasaneyī is intended (?).
{18} The correct form of the first of the names is Pavanāha; and of the second, Vāmana. The consonant
	 of the first akṣara of the latter name can also be read as c.
{19} Read -māṃtaratavāgrāmayoḥ, but the meaning of āntara is not clear in this reading. Probably what is 
	 intended is "in the neighbourhood", or "another".
{20} Both the bracketed akṣaras are engraved only in parts.
{21} The three akṣaras in the brackets show uncouth forms.
{22} That is, 77, mentioned here in Prakrit. For the Prakritism in the expression, cf. bayāsa (Sans. duāchat-
	 vāriṁśat) in the Kamauli plates of V. S. 1190, in Ep. Ind., Vol. IV, pp. 111-112.
{23} Originally, a daṇḍa, with an attempt to change it to the sign of visarga. Nibaddha means registered.
	 Cf. Ep. Ind., Vol. XIX, p. 18, 1. 16. The reading of the two preceding letters in the brackets is not
	 certain.
{24} The sense of this and the preceding word is not clear to me. The reading of the first two of these
	 akṣaras is also uncertain.
{25} This is grammatically incorrect. Read grāmau dvau dattau or grāmadvaya dattaṃ. Obviously, the same
	 villages which were donated previously. The daṇḍa in the preceding line is redundant.
{26} The akṣara in the brackets is written above the line, in smaller form.
{27} Read pārthivendrān.
{28} Read vilopyāḥ ||12|| iti |
{29} This is a contraction of Dūtaka. The consonant of hi that follows is engraved as d.
{30} Delete the daṇḍa, that read both the names as one word.
{31} The syllable in the brackets, which was originally omitted, is engraved just above the preceding letter,
	 and it also appears to have been rubbed off. 
{32} The preceding line is in bigger letter and engraved as separate from the main body, as we find also 
	 in No. 51, above. Two of the letters in the line, viz., na and rā may perhaps be explained as the 
	 initial akṣaras of nṛvarmmaṇaḥ rājñaḥ. The first of the akṣaras in the line, i. e., ra, is also found in 
	 No. 38, 1. 14.
